notice: Every case is invented test content about fictional products, outlets, and reviewers. Nothing here describes a real product or a real review.

cases.text: The Northstar Atlas 4000 is the easiest desktop recommendation we have made this year. It stayed nearly silent under a full render load, and the tool-free side panel makes upgrades painless. Next to the Aether Pro 4100 it finished our export test a few minutes sooner. The only real letdown is the front panel, which offers just two USB ports. Verdict: buy it.

pros.quote: It stayed nearly silent under a full render load
the tool-free side panel makes upgrades painless

cons.quote: the front panel, which offers just two USB ports

cases.text: We wanted to love the Northstar Beacon 5000. Its case is compact enough to sit under a monitor shelf and the bundled keyboard is genuinely good. But the fans ramp up audibly during long compiles, and the Boreal Studio 5100 costs less with the same memory. The Aether Pro 4100 remains the quieter choice. A capable machine with caveats: worth considering, not an automatic pick.

pros.quote: Its case is compact enough to sit under a monitor shelf
the bundled keyboard is genuinely good

cons.quote: the fans ramp up audibly during long compiles

cases.text: The Northstar Cobalt 3000 feels like a product from two years ago. Boot times were the slowest in our group, the single storage bay leaves no room to grow, and the power supply whined throughout testing. It does at least include a three-year warranty. The Forge W 3100 does everything here better for similar money. We cannot recommend the Cobalt.

pros.quote: It does at least include a three-year warranty

cons.quote: Boot times were the slowest in our group
the single storage bay leaves no room to grow

cases.text: After three weeks with the Northstar Delta 6000 we have very little to complain about. The front intake keeps temperatures steady without drama, cable routing is tidy out of the box, and setup took under ten minutes. We would like a longer power cable in the box. Highly recommended for small studios.

pros.quote: The front intake keeps temperatures steady without drama

cons.quote: We would like a longer power cable in the box

cases.text: The Northstar Summit 7000 has the best laptop screen we tested this quarter: bright, sharp, and easy to read outdoors. The keyboard deck flexes more than it should, though, and battery life trailed the Aether Roam 7100 by about ninety minutes in our loop. If the display matters most to you it is a fine choice; frequent travellers should look carefully at the alternatives.

pros.quote: bright, sharp, and easy to read outdoors

cons.quote: The keyboard deck flexes more than it should

cons.claim: Shorter battery life than a rival
cons.quote: battery life trailed the Aether Roam 7100 by about ninety minutes

cases.text: A second sample of the Northstar Delta 6000 fared badly in our workstation round-up. The Vector Max 6100 beat it in every sustained benchmark, and the Boreal Studio 5100 ran cooler while doing so. Our unit also arrived with a loose drive cage. The case finish resists fingerprints well, which is about the only bright spot. Skip this configuration.

pros.quote: The case finish resists fingerprints well

cons.quote: Our unit also arrived with a loose drive cage

cases.text: Northstar has confirmed that the Atlas 4000 will ship in three configurations next month. We saw a pre-production unit briefly at a press event and were not able to run any tests. Pricing puts it directly against the Aether Pro 4100. A full review will follow once a retail unit arrives.

The Northstar Summit 7000 review unit we received was a disappointment. The hinge creaked from the first day and the trackpad missed clicks along its upper edge. cases.text: The Northstar Beacon 5000 handled our vectorised maths workloads without complaint, and roaming profiles synced correctly on first login. The forged aluminium lid feels expensive. Only the Vector Max 6100 was faster, and by a small margin. The glossy screen coating shows reflections in bright rooms. An easy recommendation for office fleets.

pros.quote: The forged aluminium lid feels expensive

cons.quote: The glossy screen coating shows reflections in bright rooms

cases.text:
Northstar Cobalt 3000:  a budget tower with
old bones.

The price is hard to argue with,   and the port selection
is generous for the money. The stock cooler is loud   under
load, however.

Both the Forge W  3100 and the Aether Pro 4100 are quieter. Reasonable value if noise does not bother you; otherwise look elsewhere.

pros.quote: The price is hard to argue with
the port selection is generous for the money

cons.quote: The stock cooler is loud under load
